name: Sikagard-62
paste:
SIKAGARD®-62: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikagard®-62, July 2023, Version 04.04 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/i/sikagard_-62.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikagard®-62 where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (July 2023, Version 04.04).
1.2 Product description. Sikagard®-62 is a two part, rigid, 100 % solids, coloured high build epoxy resin based protective coating with high resistance to abrasion and chemical attack.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikagard®-62 may only be used by experienced professionals.
    - Chemical resistant protective layer on concrete, stone, cementitious mortars and renderings, epoxy cement, epoxy resin based products and steel
    - Lining in storage tanks and silos
    - Anti-corrosion for chemical bunded areas, food and beverage processing plants, sewage works, water retaining structures, chemical and pharmaceutical facilities.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.9.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikagard®-62
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: 2-PART EPOXY PROTECTIVE COATING / LINING SYSTEM
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Sustainability. Conformity with LEED v2009 IEQc 4.2: Low-Emitting Materials - Paints and Coatings
2.3 Certificates and test reports.
    - Potable Water approved to AS/NZS 4020:2018 - Testing of products for use in contact with drinking water
    - Coating for concrete protection according the requirements of EN 1504-2:2004, Declaration of Performance 0206060100100000011008, certified by FPC Notified Body and provided with CE marking
    - WRAS, test report No. M104991, 2011, Contact with water for wholesome purposes according BS 6920- 1:2000
2.4 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS/NZS 4020:2018: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - EN 1504-2:2004: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - BS 6920- 1:2000: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - DIN 5305: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shore D Hardness (p.2).
    - ASTM D 4060: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Mechanical resistance (p.2).
    - ISO 4624: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN 12944-4: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Application Instructions > Steel Surface (p.3).
    - EN 14879: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Application Instructions > Steel Surface (p.3).
2.5 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Solvent free
    - Good mechanical and chemical resistance
    - High build
    - Impervious to liquids
    - Easy to mix and to apply
2.6 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Epoxy resin
    - Appearance and colour: RAL colour range - refer to Sika colour chart
    - Density: Mixed resin ~1.37 kg/l; Density values determined at +23 °C
2.7 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Shore D Hardness: ~80 (DIN 5305)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: > 1.5 N/mm² to concrete (ISO 4624)
    - Chemical resistance: Please contact Sika technical service for specific information.
2.8 Mechanical resistance.
    | Taber Abraser | CS 10/ 1000/ | 24.4mg |
    | 1000 |
    | Taber Abraser | CS 17/ | 70 mg |
    | 1000/ 1000 |
    | Taber Abraser | H 22/ 1000/ 1000 | 560.6mg |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (ASTM D 4060)
2.9 Temperature resistance.
    | Exposure | Dry heat |
    | Permanent | +50 °C |
    | max. 7 days | +80 °C |
    | max. 12 hours | +100 °C |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
2.10 Systems. Standard Three Coat System: (DFT from 600um - 800um); Primer: Sikafloor 160 or 161 + 1st Coat: Sikagard 62 + 2nd Coat : Sikagard 62; Fibreglass Laminate System: (DFT from 1000um - 1200um) Subject to glass Thickness; Primer : Sikafloor 160, Fibreglass, Sikafloor 160 + 1st Coat: Sikagard 62 + 2nd Coat : Sikagard 62; SikaGard EpoCem 720 System: (DFT from 1200um +) Subject to EpoCem 720 Thickness; Typically used on High Wear, Damaged or High moisture content substrate applications: SikaGard EpoCem 720 + 1st Coat: Sikagard 62 + 2nd Coat : Sikagard 62 Please refer to Sikagard 720 EpoCem PDS; Please refer to individual Product Data Sheets and consult the Sika Technical Department for specific Consumption Priming and Coverage Information pertaining to project requirements.
2.11 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Shelf life: Part A: 24 months; Part B: 24 months; From date of production if stored properly.
    - Storage conditions: The packaging must be stored properly in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging, in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +30 °C. Protected from direct sunlight.
2.12 Packaging.
    | Part A | 8.4 kg |
    | Part B | 3.0 kg |
    | Sikafloor Pigment x 1 | 1.15kg |
    | Total kit 12.55kg  -  9.2 L | Total kit 12.55kg  -  9.2 L |

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (July 2023, Version 04.04) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality.
    - The substrate must be sound, clean, dry, free from contaminants such as dirt, grease, oil, old coatings, release agents, laitance and other adhesion preventing or influencing substances.
    - On high absorbent, non-sound or non cement based substrates precautions have to be taken and a suitable primer has to be used.
3.3 Substrate preparation - Concrete Substrate.
    - Concrete substrate must be prepared mechanically to achieve an open textured surface.
    - Weak areas in the substrate must be removed and surface defects such as blowholes and voids must be fully exposed.
    - All dust, loose and friable material must be completely removed from all surfaces before application of the product, preferably by brush and/or vacuum.
    - Open voids and blowholes need to be closed with a suitable Sika® pore filling mortar. The roughness of the substrate needs to be levelled with a suitable Sika® rendering and levelling mortar.
3.4 Substrate preparation - Steel Surface. Steel surface must be prepared mechanically using abrasive blast cleaning. The level SSPC-SP 10 “near white metal blast cleaned” or level Sa 2 ½ according to ISO EN 12944-4 has to be achieved. Welds and joints have to be prepared according to EN 14879, part 1. After blast cleaning remove all dust dirt and blasting material. In order to maintain the surface conditions after blast cleaning air-conditioning is recommended.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (July 2023, Version 04.04) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: Part A : Part B = 3 : 1 by weight 2.1 : 1 by volume
    - Consumption: ~0.25 - 0.35 L m² per layer depending on system structure requrements
4.3 Layer thickness. ~0.2 - 0.3 mm per layer depending on substrate condition, method application and temperature. Recommended number of coats - minimum 2 and possibly 3 depending on required film build for the given environment.
4.4 Pot Life.
    | Temperature | Time |
    | +10 °C | ~30 min |
    | +20 °C | ~20 min |
    | +30 °C | ~10 min |
4.5 Waiting time to overcoating.
    | Temperature | Min. | Max. | Full cure |
    | +10 °C | ~ 30 hours | ~ 3 days | ~ 14 days |
    | +20 °C | ~ 10 hours | ~ 2 days | ~ 10days |
    | +30 °C | ~ 6 hours | ~ 1 day | ~ 5 days |
4.6 Mixing. Prior to mixing stir Part A mechanically then add required pigment and stir for a further 1 minute, Add all Part B to Part A and mix for a further 3 minutes until a uniform mix has been achieved. Use a low speed electrical stirrer (300–400 rpm) to avoid air entrapment. To ensure proper mixing pour material into a clean container and stir again.
4.7 Application. Apply by brush, roller or airless spray.
4.8 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools with Thinner C immediately after use. Hardened and/or cured material can only be removed mechanically.
4.9 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Do not apply Sikagard®-62 on moist substrates
    - Sag resistance on vertical surface is approx. 200 μm.
    - Freshly applied Sikagard®-62 must be protected from damp, condensation and water for at least 24 hours
    - For exact colour matching ensure using material from the same control batch numbers.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +8 °C min. / +40 °C max.
5.3 Relative air humidity. < 80 %
5.4 Substrate temperature. +8 °C min. / +40 °C max. Minimum 3 °C above dew point, beware of condensation
5.5 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Shore D Hardness: ~80 (DIN 5305)
    - Mechanical resistance: Taber Abraser | CS 10/ 1000/ | 24.4mg; 1000; Taber Abraser | CS 17/ | 70 mg; 1000/ 1000; Taber Abraser | H 22/ 1000/ 1000 | 560.6mg (ASTM D 4060)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: > 1.5 N/mm² to concrete (ISO 4624)
5.6 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.7 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikagard®-62, July 2023, Version 04.04, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/i/sikagard_-62.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
